noAnchorGaps.concept: The rule of fives — by around the fifth touch the level finally breaks / gives way
noAnchorGaps.quote: by around the fifth touch there's often no one left, and the level finally gives way
noAnchorGaps.why: move horizontal_sr exposes only level(L), touch1, touch2, touch3 — there is no anchor for a later/fifth touch or the breakdown moment, so the 'gives way' climax cannot be marked without inventing an anchor

noAnchorGaps.concept: The SECOND rejection — price tests the level, gets rejected, then tests it again before breaking
noAnchorGaps.quote: price tests it, gets rejected, tests it again
noAnchorGaps.why: move sr_flip exposes only a single pre-breakout test anchor (test1), plus breakout/retest/top/level — there is no second-test point anchor, so the repeated test cannot be drawn without inventing an anchor
